nary_nodes.label: Microsoft announces 4,800 job cuts
evidence: Microsoft has announced it has cut 4,800 jobs - roughly 2.1% of its workforce - with Xbox to bear a large number of its latest layoffs.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox experiences significant layoffs
evidence: Xbox to bear a large number of its latest layoffs.
The sweeping layoffs will see more than 1,600 roles immediately axed at Xbox.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox begins significant restructure
evidence: Asha Sharma, who recently took over as Xbox's chief executive, said in a note to staff it was "beginning the most significant restructure in Xbox history".

nary_nodes.label: Four Xbox studios spun off
evidence: Four Xbox game development studios - Compulsion Games, Double Fine Productions, Ninja Theory and Undead Lab - would also be spun off as part of the changes, she added.

nary_nodes.label: Additional 1,600 Xbox roles reduced
evidence: Another 1,600 roles will be reduced from Xbox as a result.

nary_nodes.label: Industry change requires company adaptation
evidence: Amy Coleman, executive vice president at Microsoft, told employees in a memo that the tech giant needed to focus on areas that can deliver for customers amid a "fast-changing industry".
"Companies don't get to choose whether their industry changes; they only get to choose whether they change with it," she said.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox changes for a bigger future
evidence: "These changes are about a bigger future for Xbox, not a smaller one," Sharma said in a note, shared on X.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox will not mistake longevity for inevitability
evidence: "History is full of companies that mistake longevity for inevitability. We will not be one of them."
"These changes are about a bigger future for Xbox, not a smaller one," Sharma said in a note, shared on X.

nary_nodes.label: AI changes how work gets done
evidence: She noted that while the company would not replace the lost roles with AI, "what is true is that AI is changing how work gets done".

nary_nodes.label: Gaming industry faces difficult time
evidence: The announcement comes at an already difficult time in the gaming industry, with many studios still reeling from brutal layoffs in recent years.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox culled 2,000 staff in 2024
evidence: In 2024, Xbox culled more than 2,000 staff and shuttered four studios bought prior to its bumper acquisition of Call of Duty maker Activision-Blizzard.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox shuttered four studios in 2024
evidence: In 2024, Xbox culled more than 2,000 staff and shuttered four studios bought prior to its bumper acquisition of Call of Duty maker Activision-Blizzard.

nary_nodes.label: Microsoft announced 9,000 job cuts
evidence: Little more than a year later, Microsoft said it would cut up to 9,000 jobs after setting out plans to double down on its multi-billion-dollar AI spending.

nary_nodes.label: Firms hike console prices
evidence: The spiralling costs of hardware have also prompted firms including Microsoft to hike the price of years-old consoles and similar consumer gadgets

nary_nodes.label: AI data centers blamed for demand
evidence: - with many blaming AI data centres for pushing up demand too quickly for supply to catch up.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox cuts are painful but a reset is needed
evidence: Sharma said on Monday that while she knew the cuts were "painful", there was a "reset" needed across Xbox's entire content portfolio, platform and operations.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox changes mark a major reset
evidence: Tech analyst Paolo Pescatore told the BBC the changes indeed marked a "major reset" for the company, which has further trials ahead.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox challenge is defining its stand
evidence: "The challenge is not just cutting costs; it is defining what Xbox stands for in a world where games are moving across console, PC, cloud and subscription platforms," he said.

nary_nodes.label: Mojang and King report directly to Sharma
evidence: As part of Xbox's sweeping changes, Minecraft developer Mojang and Candy Crush developer King will now report directly to Sharma.

nary_nodes.label: Restructuring underlines Xbox's vision
evidence: Piers Harding-Rolls of Ampere Analysis said this restructuring "underlines Xbox's vision for its studios and content, which will be more heavily focused on the biggest IP and audiences".

nary_nodes.label: Xbox previously bought studios for Game Pass
evidence: He said the company had previously bought a plethora of studios to boost offerings on its subscription service Game Pass.

nary_nodes.label: Some teams better outside Xbox
evidence: "But the company has now decided that some of these teams and the games they are building would be better suited to sit outside the Xbox organisation," he said

nary_nodes.label: Not closing studios is positive news
evidence: - adding that its decision not close them was "positive news during a difficult time".

"But the company has now decided that some of these teams and the games they are building would be better suited to sit outside the Xbox organisation," he said - adding that its decision not close them was "positive news during a difficult time".

nary_nodes.label: Double Fine and Compulsion return to independence
evidence: Double Fine and Compulsion will both return to independent management.

nary_nodes.label: Double Fine thankful for years with Xbox
evidence: Double Fine, acquired by Microsoft in 2019, wrote on X that it was "thankful to everyone at Xbox for seven great years together".

nary_nodes.label: Double Fine grateful for outcome preserving history
evidence: The Psychonauts developer added it was grateful to have been able to reach an outcome "which preserves our history and culture, and returns ownership of our games to us".

nary_nodes.label: Studios depart with intellectual property
evidence: Both itself and Compulsion, which developed action-adventure title South of Midnight, will depart with their intellectual property (IP).
